nodes.Name: enableWER
nodes.DocComment: enableWER re-enables Windows error reporting without fault reporting UI.

nodes.Name: isAbort
nodes.DocComment:
isAbort returns true, if context r describes exception raised
by calling runtime.abort function.

go:nosplit

nodes.Name: isgoexception
nodes.DocComment:
isgoexception reports whether this exception should be translated
into a Go panic or throw.

It is nosplit to avoid growing the stack in case we're aborting
because of a stack overflow.

go:nosplit

nodes.Name: sigFetchGSafe
nodes.DocComment:
sigFetchGSafe is like getg() but without panicking
when TLS is not set.
Only implemented on windows/386, which is the only
arch that loads TLS when calling getg(). Others
use a dedicated register.

nodes.Name: sigtrampgo
nodes.DocComment:
sigtrampgo is called from the exception handler function, sigtramp,
written in assembly code.
Return EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_EXECUTION if the exception is handled,
else return EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH.

It is nosplit for the same reason as exceptionhandler.

go:nosplit

nodes.Name: exceptionhandler
nodes.DocComment:
Called by sigtramp from Windows VEH handler.
Return value signals whether the exception has been handled (EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_EXECUTION)
or should be made available to other handlers in the chain (EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH).

This is nosplit to avoid growing the stack until we've checked for
_EXCEPTION_BREAKPOINT, which is raised by abort() if we overflow the g0 stack.

go:nosplit

nodes.Name: sehhandler
nodes.DocComment:
sehhandler is reached as part of the SEH chain.

It is nosplit for the same reason as exceptionhandler.

go:nosplit

nodes.Name: firstcontinuehandler
nodes.DocComment:
It seems Windows searches ContinueHandler's list even
if ExceptionHandler returns EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_EXECUTION.
firstcontinuehandler will stop that search,
if exceptionhandler did the same earlier.

It is nosplit for the same reason as exceptionhandler.

go:nosplit

nodes.Name: lastcontinuehandler
nodes.DocComment:
lastcontinuehandler is reached, because runtime cannot handle
current exception. lastcontinuehandler will print crash info and exit.

It is nosplit for the same reason as exceptionhandler.

go:nosplit

Children.Name: if
Children.RawSource: GOARCH == "arm64" && info.ExceptionCode == windows.EXCEPTION_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION && (r.PC() < firstmoduledata.text || firstmoduledata.etext < r.PC())

nodes.Name: winthrow
nodes.DocComment:
Always called on g0. gp is the G where the exception occurred.

go:nosplit

nodes.Name: dieFromException
nodes.DocComment:
dieFromException raises an exception that bypasses all exception handlers.
This provides the expected exit status for the shell.
